text: Extending scalars R→A sends a right coaction ρ:M→M⊗H to id_A⊗ρ, followed by the tensor identification with (A⊗M)⊗_A(A⊗H). Thus both the carrier and coefficient coalgebra change. The identification uses [Stacks, tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); the source proves the additional coalgebra compatibility without any flatness or finite-generation hypothesis. Checks pass: [baseChangeCoact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L71), [baseChange_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L192).
Evaluates the candidate on pure tensors.
For the regular comodule this agrees with the extended coproduct.

If ρ(m)=Σm₀⊗m₁, the extended coaction sends a⊗m to Σ(a⊗m₀)⊗(1⊗m₁). The scalar a remains in the carrier factor, while the coefficient receives 1. This is the elementary-tensor formula supplied by [Stacks, tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); no chosen basis or unique tensor decomposition is asserted. Checks pass: [baseChange_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L192), [baseChange_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L184).
The regular-coaction specialization matches coalgebra base change.
The packaged comodule selects this candidate map.

The extended module A⊗M becomes a right comodule over A⊗H, with both coaction laws inherited through tensor associativity. This implements the coaction axioms of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) after scalar extension. Commutative semirings suffice; the explicit structure selects this coaction and does not require M→A⊗M to be injective. Checks pass: [baseChange_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L184), [baseChange_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L192).
The constructed structure retains the stated candidate map.
The regular comodule recovers the extended coalgebra.

This equation identifies the coaction stored in the selected scalar-extended comodule with the explicit tensor composite id_A⊗ρ followed by reassociation. It exposes the actual structure satisfying [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), rather than claiming every coaction on A⊗M is the same. The coefficient coalgebra is A⊗H over A, not H over R. Checks pass: [baseChangeCoact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L71), [baseChange_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L192).
The identified map has the expected pure-tensor formula.
Its regular-comodule case agrees with the extended coproduct.

A comodule morphism f:M→N extends to id_A⊗f between the scalar-extended comodules. Tensoring its intertwining equation proves that it still preserves coactions, as required by [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). This construction needs commutative scalar semirings but neither flatness nor injectivity or surjectivity of f; it does not assert preservation of those properties. Checks pass: [baseChange_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L236), [baseChange_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L246).
The construction preserves identity morphisms.
It preserves composition in the correct order.

Forgetting the compatibility proof from the extended comodule morphism leaves exactly id_A⊗f. Thus the morphism operation adds no extra transformation of either tensor factor. The source proves the coaction equation of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); the underlying scalar extension acts on vectors by a⊗m↦a⊗f(m), without any freeness assumption. Checks pass: [baseChange_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L260), [baseChange_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L246).
Evaluates the underlying extended map.
The same underlying operation preserves composition.

The scalar-extended morphism sends a⊗m to a⊗f(m), keeping the scalar factor unchanged. Elementary tensors generate the tensor module, so this determines the entire linear map. Its bundled coaction compatibility is the morphism condition of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); the formula does not assume every tensor is itself elementary. Checks pass: [baseChange_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L228), [baseChange_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/BaseChange.lean#L236).
Identifies the full map with linear scalar extension.
The identity specialization fixes every tensor.

For an A⊗C-comodule M over A, tensor cancellation turns its coaction into an R-linear map M→M⊗_R C. Explicitly, m⊗_A(a⊗c) becomes (am)⊗_R c. This is the unit-and-associativity identification of [Stacks, tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); compatible R- and A-actions are supplied, and no inverse to R→A is needed. Checks pass: [restrictScalarsCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L56), [rid_counit_cancelBaseChange](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/BaseChange.lean#L101).
The map is the original coaction followed by cancellation.
Cancellation respects contraction by the counit.

Tensor cancellation equips the same underlying module M with a right C-coaction over R. The source transports coassociativity and the counit equation through this isomorphism, matching [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). Restriction changes the scalars and coefficient coalgebra, not the elements of M; it assumes compatible scalar actions, without a flatness hypothesis. Checks pass: [restrictScalars_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L105), [restrictScalarsCoact_eq_tmul_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L112).
The constructed coaction is exactly the cancellation composite.
Cancellation preserves each specified pure-coaction equation.

The restricted equation ρ_R(m)=m⊗c holds exactly when the original equation is ρ_A(m)=m⊗(1⊗c). Applying the inverse tensor cancellation proves both directions. The identification is governed by [Stacks, tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); c is any coefficient element, so the theorem does not silently assume that c is group-like or a character. Checks pass: [restrictScalarsCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L56), [mem_fixedSubcomodule_restrictScalars_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L121).
Exposes the cancellation map used in the equivalence.
The specialization at c=1 preserves fixed-vector membership.

Fixed-vector membership means precisely ρ(m)=m⊗1. Tensor cancellation and the identity 1=1⊗1 in the extended coefficient object make this condition unchanged on restriction. The tensor identification follows [Stacks, tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). Only a distinguished coefficient element 1 is required here; no Hopf multiplication or group-action interpretation is assumed by this lemma. Checks pass: [restrictScalarsCoact_eq_tmul_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L112), [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L75).
The general coefficient equation specializes to c=1.
The native fixed predicate is exactly the stated coaction equation.

An A-linear morphism preserving the A⊗C-coactions remains a C-comodule morphism after restricting scalars to R. Its function is unchanged; cancellation commutes with applying f to the carrier factor. This proves the intertwining condition of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) for the restricted coactions, rather than treating an arbitrary R-linear map as compatible. Checks pass: [restrictScalars_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L148), [restrictScalars_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L156).
The underlying map is scalar restriction of f.
The value at every vector remains f(m).

This functor first forgets the coaction, then sends M to the A-module A⊗_R M and f to id_A⊗f. Its target is the module category, so no new coaction is assigned. It combines the forgetful functor of [Wisbauer §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) with tensor extension; A may be a noncommutative R-algebra. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L63), [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L69).
The object is the indicated tensor semimodule.
The arrow is precisely scalar extension of the underlying map.

The object assigned to M is exactly the semimodule A⊗_R M, with A acting on the first factor. The coaction is forgotten, consistent with the underlying-object functor in [Wisbauer §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). This object equation makes no finiteness assumption and gives no injectivity claim for the canonical map m↦1⊗m. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L69).
The object identification supports the corresponding map formula.

The functor sends f to id_A⊗f, after the displayed identifications of its source and target tensor modules. The surrounding equality-induced arrows only align those objects; they add no mathematical transformation. This is scalar extension after the forgetful functor of [Wisbauer §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), retaining the scalar factor and forgetting the coaction data. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L63).
The equality-induced arrows identify precisely the tensor module objects.

A linear equivalence e:M→N transports the coaction by ρ_N=(e⊗id_C)ρ_M e⁻¹. This makes e satisfy the comodule-morphism equation of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). It constructs a chosen coaction on N; it does not claim that an arbitrary previously given coaction on N is preserved by every linear equivalence. Checks pass: [transportCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L53), [transportCoact_refl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L61).
Evaluation gives exactly the conjugation formula.
Transport along the identity returns the original coaction.

The conjugated map (e⊗id_C)ρ_M e⁻¹ satisfies coassociativity and the counit law because e and e⁻¹ cancel. Hence it supplies the right-comodule structure required by [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The structure is selected explicitly, allowing other coactions on N; no basis, finite dimension, or multiplication on C is needed. Checks pass: [transport_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L89), [transportCoact_trans](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L100).
The structure uses the specified conjugated coaction.
Successive transport agrees with transport along the composite equivalence.

Transporting a comodule morphism f along equivalences e_M and e_N gives e_N∘f∘e_M⁻¹ between the transported coactions. Substituting their conjugation formulas proves the intertwining equation in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The two equivalences need only be linear because the target coactions are constructed from them, not independently prescribed. Checks pass: [transportHom_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L145), [transportHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L160).
Transport takes identity morphisms to identities.
Conjugation preserves composition of comodule morphisms.

The transported morphism has underlying linear map e_N∘f∘e_M⁻¹, in that order. This exposes the conjugation used to satisfy the compatibility diagram of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The inverse acts on the source before f, and the target equivalence acts afterward; there is no transpose, dualization, or change of coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [transportHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L136), [transportHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L160).
The vector formula confirms the composition order.
Composing transported maps cancels the intermediate equivalence.

The equivalence e itself becomes a comodule morphism from M to N equipped with the transported coaction. The identity ρ_Ne=(e⊗id_C)ρ_M follows by cancellation of e⁻¹e, exactly the condition in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The target structure is specified locally; compatibility with any other coaction on N is not asserted. Checks pass: [transportToHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L215), [transportIso_hom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L259).
The morphism acts by the original equivalence e.
The bundled categorical isomorphism has the same forward linear map.

The inverse equivalence e⁻¹ is a comodule morphism from the transported structure on N back to M. Rearranging the conjugation equation proves its compatibility, as in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). This constructs an actual inverse to the forward transport map; it requires only linear invertibility, without assuming an antipode or finite dimension. Checks pass: [transportInvHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L222), [transportIso_inv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L265).
The inverse morphism evaluates by e⁻¹.
The categorical inverse has this underlying linear map.

Forgetting the comodule compatibility proof from the forward transport morphism returns exactly e. Thus transport packages the original linear equivalence into a morphism for the new coaction, satisfying [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), without changing its values. The equation concerns the explicitly transported target structure and does not identify arbitrary coactions on N. Checks pass: [transportToHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L215), [transportIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L271).
Evaluation is precisely e(m).
The forward categorical isomorphism evaluates the same way.

The underlying linear map of the inverse transport morphism is e⁻¹. The extra bundled field only certifies the coaction compatibility of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); it does not alter the inverse function. Its domain uses the transported coaction, so this statement gives no automatic compatibility for an independently chosen comodule structure on N. Checks pass: [transportInvHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L222), [transportIso_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L277).
Evaluation agrees with the inverse linear equivalence.
The categorical inverse has the same values.

At each vector m, the forward transport morphism evaluates to e(m). This confirms that the coaction-preserving map is the original equivalence with the compatibility proof prescribed by [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The transported structure changes how N coacts; it does not modify the equivalence or introduce a choice of basis. Checks pass: [transportToHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L199), [transportIso_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L271).
The entire underlying linear map equals e.
The isomorphism packaging preserves this evaluation formula.

At each vector n, the inverse transport morphism evaluates to e⁻¹(n). Together with the forward construction this realizes an isomorphism of comodules in the sense of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The inverse is already supplied by the linear equivalence; the construction proves its coaction compatibility rather than choosing a new inverse. Checks pass: [transportInvHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L207), [transportIso_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L277).
The underlying linear map is exactly e⁻¹.
The categorical inverse preserves the same evaluation formula.

Converting a product of extended nonnegative reals to a real equals the product of their converted values, even when infinity occurs. This works because infinity converts to zero and 0·∞=0: a product involving infinity is either zero or infinity, and both convert to zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L337).

Clipping a real product at zero agrees with multiplying the clipped factors when the first factor is nonnegative. The second factor may be negative; then both sides are zero. Without the sign hypothesis, two negative factors give a positive product although each clipped factor is zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L297).

Converting an extended reciprocal to a real equals taking the real reciprocal after conversion. Positive finite values behave ordinarily. At zero and infinity the equality also holds: extended reciprocal exchanges those two values, both convert to zero, and Lean defines the real reciprocal of zero as zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L975).

Division commutes with conversion to real numbers without finiteness or nonzero-denominator assumptions. The exceptional values agree after conversion: for example, extended 5/0 is infinity and converts to zero, matching Lean’s real 5/0=0. This is compatibility of two total definitions, not ordinary division by zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L978).

For a strictly positive real number, converting its reciprocal to [0,∞] agrees with taking the extended reciprocal of its conversion. Strict positivity matters: at zero the converted real reciprocal is zero, whereas the extended reciprocal of zero is infinity. Negative inputs likewise do not satisfy the asserted equality. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L946).

With a strictly positive real denominator, converting the real quotient to [0,∞] equals dividing the converted numerator by the converted denominator. The numerator can be negative, in which case both sides are zero. Allowing a zero denominator would fail, for example with numerator one: zero versus infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L961).

An inequality a≤b between extended nonnegative reals remains true after conversion to real numbers provided b is finite. This also forces a to be finite, so no separate assumption on a is needed. Without the upper-value restriction, 1≤∞ would incorrectly become 1≤0. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L67).

An extended nonnegative real converts to a strictly positive real when it is neither zero nor infinity. These two exclusions account for both exceptional zero outputs of the conversion. In particular, infinity is positive in the extended order but its converted real value is zero, so finiteness cannot be omitted. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L133).

For two finite extended nonnegative reals, converting their sum to a real gives the sum of their real values. Both finiteness assumptions prevent the conversion’s infinity-to-zero default from breaking additivity: infinity+1 converts to zero, whereas converting the summands first gives 0+1=1. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L41).

A nonnegative real is recovered by converting it to [0,∞] and then back to a real. The nonnegativity hypothesis is essential because the first conversion clips negative inputs to zero. More generally, the composite is max(r,0), so a negative input does not survive this round trip. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L253).

A finite extended nonnegative real is recovered by converting it to a real and then back. Finiteness is the only extra assumption; nonnegativity is already built into the domain. Infinity is excluded because conversion to a real sends it to zero, which converts back to zero rather than infinity. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L249).

Converting a sum of two nonnegative real numbers to [0,∞] agrees with adding their conversions. Here clipping changes neither summand nor their sum. The sign assumptions exclude cancellation between positive and negative terms: for 1 and −1, converting the sum gives zero while adding the conversions gives one. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L52).

The positive part of a sum is at most the sum of the positive parts, so conversion to [0,∞] is subadditive for arbitrary real inputs. No sign hypotheses are needed. Equality can fail when signs oppose: 1+(−1) converts to zero, but the separate conversions sum to one. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L57).

For a nonnegative real base and a natural-number exponent, conversion to [0,∞] commutes with taking powers. The exponent may be zero, with every zeroth power, including 0⁰, defined as one. Negative bases cannot be allowed uniformly: squaring −1 gives one before conversion but zero after clipping first. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L306).

Conversion to real numbers preserves natural-number powers of every extended nonnegative value, including infinity. For a positive exponent, infinity’s power is infinity and converts to zero, matching the corresponding power of its converted value zero. At exponent zero both sides are one, using the convention 0⁰=1. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L343).

When the subtrahend q is nonnegative, converting the real difference p−q agrees with subtracting the converted values using truncated subtraction. The minuend p may be negative; then both sides are zero. If q were negative, the equality could fail: p=0,q=−1 gives one on the left and zero on the right. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L443).

For finite extended nonnegative reals, comparison after conversion to real numbers is equivalent to the original comparison. The equivalence preserves and reflects order. Finiteness is essential for this general statement because infinity converts to zero: for example, infinity’s converted value is below one even though infinity itself is not. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L61).

For two finite extended nonnegative reals, strict comparison is equivalent to strict comparison of their converted real values. Neither zero nor equality needs exclusion; the statement handles both correctly. Infinity must be excluded because it converts to zero: infinity’s converted value is less than one although infinity itself is greater. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L76).

Converting real numbers to [0,∞] preserves non-strict inequalities, because replacing each input by max(r,0) is monotone. No nonnegativity hypothesis is needed. The conversion does not preserve every strict inequality or reflect order on all reals: distinct negative inputs are both sent to zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L137).

A real number converts to zero in [0,∞] exactly when it is nonpositive. This includes every negative number as well as zero, since conversion takes max(r,0). Thus a zero converted value does not imply that the original real was zero; positive inputs are precisely those with nonzero conversions. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L181).

Every continuous self-map of the closed unit ball in ℝⁿ has a fixed point, including n=0, when the ball is a singleton. The categorical arrow includes continuity, and the point lies in the ball with its inherited topology. The ray construction fixes the boundary and uses division only where its denominator is nonzero. See [Hatcher, Corollary2.15, pp.114–115](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The actual disk-boundary obstruction used by the fixed-point proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/BrouwerFixedPoint.lean#L67), [The explicit ray formula lands on the unit sphere when x≠y](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SphereRay.lean#L81), [The computed ray retraction fixes every boundary point](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SphereRay.lean#L148).

There are no continuous maps i:∂Dⁿ→Dⁿ and r:Dⁿ→∂Dⁿ with r∘i the identity. This includes any possible section i, hence the usual boundary inclusion. The ball and sphere have their inherited Euclidean topologies; at n=0 the ball is a point and its boundary is empty, so even r cannot exist. See [Hatcher, Corollary2.15, pp.114–115](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The actual lifted Euclidean disk is contractible in every dimension](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Disk.lean#L58), [Reduced homology vanishes on the actual contractible disk](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Contractible.lean#L73).

For positive n, this is the distribution of the arithmetic mean of n independent uniform variables on [0,1]: it pushes their sum’s law forward by x↦x/n. Division is in ℝ. At n=0 an explicit branch gives the zero measure, so the undefined empty average is not treated as a probability distribution. See [Rudolph–Wessing, p.341](https://informatica.vu.lt/journal/INFORMATICA/article/807/file/pdf). Native Checks pass: [Order0 is the zero measure](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Bates/Basic.lean#L50), [Order1 is unit uniform](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Bates/Basic.lean#L75), [The actual independent product sample-average pushforward equals the defined law](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Bates/Basic.lean#L95), [The law of any nonempty finite independent uniform average is Bates](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Bates/Basic.lean#L299).

A finite basis makes B a finite free A-algebra; its discriminant is det(Tr(bᵢbⱼ)). Requiring that determinant to be invertible is the affine criterion in [Stacks 0BJF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BJF). Checks: [dual numbers](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Etale/Discriminant.lean#L152) have discriminant zero and are not étale. The existing [quadratic basis computation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/QuadraticAlgebra.lean#L67) gives b²+4a; setting b=0 and a=d models A[x]/(x²−d) and gives 4d. Over ℤ_(p), odd p makes 4 a unit, so [the localization unit criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/AtPrime/Basic.lean#L154) gives the requested unit-d and nonunit-d=p cases. Applying the reviewed equivalence gives their étaleness conclusions. These are specializations of existing computed families, not a separately compiled test.
